title: [Feature][Ops] Add Triton cache adapters for CANN pooled indexing
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds three fused Triton adapters for the BF16 GLM-5.3-Flash CANN KeyPool/PoolKeyIndexer integration in #16730. CANN performs pooling and index selection; these adapters translate vLLM's paged metadata, persistent caches and SFA index layout at the operator boundaries.

- **Metadata and tail addressing:** `_build_keypool_metadata_kernel` builds pooled lengths, query boundaries, compact cache slots, tail history/write addresses and MTP retained rows. DSA-CP additionally receives rank-local query boundaries and causal prefix lengths. Both metadata and tail preparation reuse this kernel.
- **Cache writes:** `_write_keypool_caches_kernel` updates the BF16 pooled cache and FP32 tail key/gate cache in one launch, using CANN state outputs or the speculative input rows as appropriate.
- **Index packing:** `_pack_indices_kernel` combines selected history indices with the unpooled causal tail, writes the existing SFA output buffer and masks graph-padding rows with `-1`.

The kernels write preallocated buffers, honor tensor strides and invalid slots, and avoid device-to-host count extraction. Metadata tiles adapt to workload size while request inversion is bounded to fit Ascend unified buffer storage. Runtime request/token counts, tail row width and input row stride are not specialization keys. Request inversion and tail column tiles are fixed by the serving layout; metadata token tiles retain four bounded sizes (8/16/32/64).

The follow-up AscendC integration is #16730, which calls the image-provided CANN KeyPool/PoolKeyIndexer operators and selects the GLM pooled-indexer backend. This PR supplies the three Triton boundary adapters; full-model use requires both PRs.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Provides the three adapters required by #16730; it does not select the model backend itself. This PR supports BF16 pooled indexing, including MTP and DSA-CP metadata. FP8 LI cache support remains in its separate PR. SFA's FP8/FP16 cache formats and attention kernels are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Five wrapper mock tests cover launch parameters and buffer reuse. Eleven real NPU operator tests cover cache writes, index packing, metadata padding, DSA-CP boundaries and graph replay.

Current revision: all 16 operator/wrapper tests passed on A5/CANN 9.2.0 (Triton Ascend 3.2.2), including changing widths/strides and graph replay. The actual Ascend JIT binder reduced the tested cache-width, tail-width, request-tile and position-alignment key counts from 4/4/8/2 to 1/1/1/1. Four metadata cases, including 65,536 tokens with 128 and 257 requests, matched the pre-specialization-change adapter outputs exactly. Current-head pre-commit and mypy passed. This revision has no new full-model accuracy/performance result. Warm operator comparison against previous PR head `8f8cf126` (64 calls per graph, 7 alternating rounds): 8K/8-request metadata 19.96 → 26.34 μs (+6.38 μs / +32%) with the fixed 128-request tile; 64K/128 requests stayed within 0.06%. MTP tail (64 requests) increased 0.30 μs; cache writes and index packing changed by less than 0.04 μs across the selected cases. All 9 cases matched exactly. Compilation and full-model execution are excluded.

Earlier joint full-model performance with #16730 + #18295 on A5/CANN 9.2.0, TP8/EP/MTP3, BF16 indexer and FP8 SFA cache, using `vllm bench serve` (vLLM `0.30.0+empty`), 256 output tokens, seed 1024 and temperature 0. Reference: frozen main [`05fa3be5`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/05fa3be5f50306a151d4863735d3d84ce63dc0a2). Each case/arm ran once without active profiling; all requests succeeded with exact lengths and no KV preemption.

| Input / concurrency / requests | Output tokens/s (main → combined) | Throughput Δ | Mean TTFT Δ | Mean TPOT Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 / C8 / 64 | 340.033 → 443.616 | +30.46% | −7.46% | −25.58% |
| 4096 / C64 / 128 | 676.309 → 737.094 | +8.99% | −6.74% | −4.29% |
| 4096 / C90 / 180 | 712.100 → 724.663 | +1.76% | +0.22% | −2.39% |
| 65536 / C8 / 16 | 40.798 → 49.467 | +21.25% | −17.65% | −15.10% |
| 1048576 / C4 / 8 | 0.873 → 1.998 | +128.80% | −55.44% | −57.64% |

Output throughput includes prefill and queueing. The candidate also contains newer upstream changes, so these results do not isolate CANN or Triton gains. At 1M, mean TTFT was 647.24 → 288.41 s and mean TPOT 1897.44 → 803.83 ms; client C4 reached peak running 3 on both arms. Both arms extended the native total-token limit by 256 to allow output (`max_model_len`/`max_position_embeddings=1048832`, unchanged RoPE). This is not 1M semantic accuracy validation; the separate C1 rank-0 profile is excluded from these measurements.

The earlier combined main CANN/Triton implementation completed two full GSM8K runs per arm (1319 questions, C64, temperature 0, seed 1024, max_tokens 4096). Raw scores: candidate 1267/1272, frozen main 05fa 1264/1269; no request errors or truncated outputs. Each paired difference was +0.227 percentage points (18 gained, 15 lost after the same format audit; exact paired p=0.728), within the 0.379-point repeat variation. This does not establish an accuracy improvement or isolate Triton effects. These full-model measurements precede the latest runtime-parameter and MTP tail-address revisions; current-head full-model accuracy remains pending.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b
